hook_text: Thirty degrees, sticky air and a thunderstorm every afternoon. Every month. Where on Earth is that?
clip_script: A voice note from the Congo Basin: it is nine in the morning, already hot and steamy. By lunchtime, huge clouds are building. At three o'clock, the rain thunders down. By evening, the forest drips and steams again. Tomorrow, the same. Tropical rainforests lie near the equator in South America, Africa and Southeast Asia. Their climate graph shows a flat temperature line and tall rain bars in every month.
visual_style: Whiteboard world map with green patches along the equator, then a climate graph with tall blue bars every month and a nearly flat red line.
mood: Warm and wonder-filled, like stepping into a giant greenhouse.
pacing: A slow, steamy start, then a clear tour of the map and a step-by-step climate graph reading.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the three biggest rainforest areas on a world map in your atlas.
